title: GitHub - Yuix-Networks/claude-orchestrator: Run Claude Desktop as many independent instances on macOS — separate profiles, accounts, sessions and working directories
excerpt: Run Claude Desktop as many independent instances on macOS — separate profiles, accounts, sessions and working directories - Yuix-Networks/claude-orchestrator
content_html:
Run Claude Desktop as many independent instances as you want on macOS — each with its own profile, account, sessions, Claude Code config and working directory.

claude-orchestrator never copies, patches or re-signs /Applications/Claude.app. It launches the original, signed app with a different data directory, so code signature, notarization, permissions and the built-in updater all keep working.

claude-orchestrator new work --workdir ~/workspace/my-project
claude-orchestrator start work
claude-orchestrator list

Or run claude-orchestrator with no arguments and do all of it from a menu (see Interactive mode).

Renamed in v0.2.0: claude-ctl is now claude-orchestrator, because the tool manages sessions as well as instances. The data directory stays at ~/Library/Application Support/claude-ctl/, so existing instances keep working.

Quick start: one instance per account

Keep work, school and a second work account signed in side by side:

claude-orchestrator new work
claude-orchestrator new school
claude-orchestrator new client --workdir ~/workspace/client   # optional default project

claude-orchestrator signin work --exclusive     # sign in, one instance at a time
claude-orchestrator signin school --exclusive
claude-orchestrator signin client --exclusive

claude-orchestrator project import --from default   # reuse the projects you already have
claude-orchestrator project add ~/workspace/api       # or add new ones: every instance gets them

claude-orchestrator start work && claude-orchestrator start school && claude-orchestrator start client
claude-orchestrator agent --install             # menu bar icons to start/stop/switch

signin --exclusive closes the other instances while you sign in, because the browser hands the login back through a single claude:// link that only one running Claude can receive. It reopens them when you press Enter.

Interactive mode

Run the command with no arguments in a terminal:

claude-orchestrator

Everything day-to-day can be done from the menu. You don't need to remember commands, session ids or file paths:

Claude Orchestrator
───────────────────────────────────────
❯ Work        ● running
  Personal    ● running
  School      ○ stopped   not logged in
───────────────────────────────────────
  + New profile
  Projects…

What you can do

Screen Options
Home Every profile with running / stopped, and a warning when it is not logged in. Below them: + New profile and Projects…
Profile (logged in) Start, or Stop / Restart when it is running · Sessions… · Log in again…
Profile (not logged in) Log in only. The other options appear after you log in
Sessions… The profile's sessions, newest first. Type to fuzzy-filter by title, account or project folder
A session Its details (account, project, start, last activity, messages, size, id) · Copy to… · Move to…
+ New profile Asks for a name, creates the profile and opens its menu so you can log in right away
Projects… The registered projects and their state in each profile · + Add project · Apply a projects.json… · Export to a projects.json… · Sync all profiles · Import from a profile…
A project Its folders, permission mode and per-profile state · Remove…

Keys: ↑/↓ (or Ctrl-P / Ctrl-N) to move, Enter to choose, Esc to go back (in a search box, Esc clears the text first), q on the home screen to quit, Ctrl-U to clear a search or text field, Ctrl-C to cancel.

What happens behind the screens:

  • Log in / Log in again… run the signin --exclusive flow. After you confirm, the other running instances are closed while you log in, so the browser's claude:// link comes back to the right window. They are reopened when you press Enter. Use Log in again… when a login has expired or the profile should use a different account.
  • Copy to… / Move to… ask for the target account (skipped when there is only one other account), then show what will happen and wait for y. Instances that have to be closed are shut down one after the other, the session is transferred, and they are reopened even if the transfer fails. A copy closes only the target and the source keeps its session. A move closes both and keeps the original as a backup.
  • Anything that writes (logging in, transfers, project changes) asks for confirmation first, then prints the same report as the matching command and waits for Enter.
  • The menu refuses to close an instance it is running inside (for example a terminal in Claude's Code tab), because that would end the menu halfway through. Run it from a regular terminal such as Terminal or iTerm.

Setting up projects from a JSON file

A project is a folder that shows up as an environment in the Code tab of every profile. Instead of adding them one by one, describe them in a file and apply it:

  1. Copy the example file and edit the paths:

    mkdir -p ~/.config/claude-orchestrator
cp examples/projects.json ~/.config/claude-orchestrator/projects.json

    examples/projects.json shows every option: a minimal entry, a custom name, extra folders, a per-project permission mode and shared defaults. If you already have projects, Projects… → Export to a projects.json… writes them to the file so you can start from there.

  2. Open Projects… → Apply a projects.json…. The default path is already filled in. Press Enter.

  3. Check the preview. The file is checked as a whole first, and every problem (a missing folder, a duplicate name, a misspelled key) is listed at once. Nothing changes until the file is clean.

    Apply ~/.config/claude-orchestrator/projects.json

  + website  ~/workspace/website
  + Mobile app  ~/workspace/mobile/app
  ~ api → API
  - old-project  (not in the file)

❯ Apply changes
  Apply and remove the 1 not in the file
  Cancel

    + is added, ~ is changed or renamed, and - is registered but missing from the file. Apply changes keeps those. Apply and remove… deletes them, which makes the registry match the file exactly.

  4. The projects are written to every profile. A profile that has not logged in yet gets them on its first start after login. The Projects… list shows where each project stands: ✓ in sync, ✗ missing (fix it with Sync all profiles), … waiting for the first login.

The same file works without the menu (project apply --dry-run, project apply, project apply --prune). See Keeping the list in a file for the full format and the details of how Claude Desktop stores environments.

Trying it safely

Set CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_HOME to point any command, the menu included, at a separate data directory. You can then experiment without touching your real profiles:

CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_HOME=/tmp/co-test claude-orchestrator

Why

Claude Desktop stores everything in a single Electron profile, so a second launch either reuses the first one's session or refuses to start. Copying the app bundle works, but the copy falls behind on updates and has to be rebuilt every time.

claude-orchestrator uses the mechanism Claude already ships for this:

What How
Separate Electron profile (cookies, sessions, settings) --user-data-dir=<per-instance path>
Separate Claude Code config (~/.claude, sessions) CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<per-instance path>
Separate Dock tile open -n (new application instance)

The result: several Claude instances side by side, each working on a different project.

Install

Install script (recommended)

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yuix-Networks/claude-orchestrator/main/install.sh | sh

The script downloads the latest release and checks its SHA-256 against the published value. It installs into /usr/local/bin when that is writable and into ~/.local/bin otherwise. It never uses sudo.

  • To pick a version or a directory, set CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_VERSION=0.2.2 or CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_DIR=~/bin in front of sh.
  • To uninstall, run curl -fsSL …/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall. Instance data is kept.

Homebrew

Recent Homebrew versions refuse to load formulae from a third-party tap until you trust it. Trust the tap before installing:

brew tap yuix-networks/tap
brew trust yuix-networks/tap
brew install yuix-networks/tap/claude-orchestrator

The formula lives in Yuix-Networks/homebrew-tap. Upgrade later with brew upgrade claude-orchestrator.

From a release

Download claude-orchestrator-<version>.tar.gz from Releases, extract it and put the binary on your PATH.

From source

swift build -c release
cp .build/release/claude-orchestrator /usr/local/bin/

Requirements: macOS 13 (Ventura) or later — open --env is needed to pass the per-instance environment. Claude Desktop must be installed in /Applications.

Commands

Command What it does
claude-orchestrator Interactive menu: profiles, sessions, projects (see Interactive mode)
claude-orchestrator version Print the version
claude-orchestrator new <name> [--workdir <path>] [--sessions-from <instance>] Create an instance; optionally seed a default project and copy another instance's sessions
claude-orchestrator start <name> [--folder <path>] Start the instance (separate profile + config)
claude-orchestrator stop <name> Stop the instance (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL if needed)
claude-orchestrator list [--json] All instances with state, pid and workdir
claude-orchestrator status <name> [--json] Details for one instance
claude-orchestrator logs <name> [-n N] [-f] Instance log lines (-f follows, survives log rotation)
claude-orchestrator open <name> [--target workdir|profile] Open a folder in Finder
claude-orchestrator signin <name> [--restart] [--exclusive] Sign-in guide; --exclusive closes the other instances while you sign in
claude-orchestrator doctor [<name>] [--json] Health checks: app version, profile, lock, disk, workdir, session
claude-orchestrator clone <name> --as <new> [--workdir <path>] Copy an instance with its profile, config and sessions
claude-orchestrator project apply [<file>] Apply a hand-edited projects.json to every instance
claude-orchestrator memory link|unlink|status Share ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md with every instance
claude-orchestrator project … (alias env) Projects shared by every instance — Claude Desktop calls them environments (see below)
claude-orchestrator session … List, inspect, copy and move Claude Code sessions (see below)
claude-orchestrator remove <name> [--purge [--permanent]] [--force] [--yes] Delete the instance (alias delete, rm). --purge moves its data to the Trash and --permanent deletes it for good. A running instance is stopped after you confirm, or right away with --force
claude-orchestrator agent [--install|--uninstall] Menu bar icons (one per instance), installable as a login item

Every --json output carries a schemaVersion field (currently 1). It is bumped only when a field is removed or renamed.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 runtime error, 2 usage error.

Projects (environments) in every instance

Claude Desktop keeps the Code tab's environments per profile and per account. Without help, you'd create every project again in each instance. project keeps one list and writes it into all of them:

claude-orchestrator project add ~/workspace/api                       # name = folder name
claude-orchestrator project add ~/workspace/site --name "Site" --folder ~/workspace/shared
claude-orchestrator project import --from default    # take over the regular Claude's environments
claude-orchestrator project list                     # ✓ synced  ✗ missing  … waiting for sign-in
claude-orchestrator project sync                     # re-apply to every instance
claude-orchestrator project remove "Site"            # also removes it from the instances (--keep: don't)
  • The list lives in config.json. New instances get it automatically, and every start applies it again.

Keeping the list in a file

You can edit the list by hand in a JSON file and apply it, from the menu (Projects… → Apply a projects.json…, see Setting up projects from a JSON file) or with project apply. The default file is ~/.config/claude-orchestrator/projects.json. A fully commented example is in examples/projects.json. The smallest useful file:

{
  "projects": [
    { "name": "shop", "path": "~/workspace/shop/shop-backend",
      "folders": ["~/workspace/shop/shop-frontend"] },
    { "path": "~/workspace/blog" }
  ]
}
claude-orchestrator project export ~/.config/claude-orchestrator/projects.json  # start from what you have
claude-orchestrator project apply --dry-run    # show the plan, change nothing
claude-orchestrator project apply              # add, update and rename projects
claude-orchestrator project apply --prune      # also delete projects that are no longer in the file

  • name and folders are optional. Paths may use ~ or be relative to the file.

  • defaults applies to every project. defaults.folders is added to each project's extra folders (for example a knowledge-base repo every session should see), and defaults.permissionMode is used where a project doesn't set its own:

    {
  "defaults": { "folders": ["~/workspace/notes"], "permissionMode": "bypassPermissions" },
  "projects": [ { "path": "~/workspace/blog", "permissionMode": "acceptEdits" } ]
}

  • permissionMode sets the default permission mode for sessions started in that project's folder. It can be default, acceptEdits, plan, auto or bypassPermissions. Claude Desktop stores this per account and per folder. For bypassPermissions, apply also turns on "allow bypass mode" and records the account's opt-in.

    • An organization policy that disables bypass mode is left alone, and the output names the affected accounts.
    • Removing permissionMode from the file clears it from Desktop. A change that only touches the mode keeps the environment's other settings.

  • // comments and trailing commas are accepted.

  • The whole file is checked first: every missing folder, duplicate name and misspelled key is reported together, and nothing changes until the file is clean.

  • Without --prune, projects missing from the file stay registered. The plan lists them.

  • A project whose folder, extra folders or name changed has its environment rewritten in every instance. That resets Desktop settings such as the model for that environment.

  • An environment belongs to an account, so before the first sign-in only the folder is trusted. The environment itself is written on the first start after you sign in. In a profile that has seen several accounts, every account gets the project.

  • An environment that already exists for the same folder is left alone, including its name, model and other settings.

  • Claude reads the list file only once per account. Claude Desktop keeps environments in its own UI storage (the profile's Local Storage). It imports ccd-session-presets.json the first time the account opens in that profile, then overwrites the file with its own list. So:

    • Projects written before the first sign-in show up on their own.
    • In an instance that has already been opened, stop it and run claude-orchestrator project sync --reset-desktop (or project apply --reset-desktop). This moves the profile's Local Storage to Local Storage.bak-<time> and writes the full list, and Claude imports it on the next start.
    • Sign-in is not affected, since cookies live elsewhere. The instance does lose its UI preferences, such as sidebar layout and dismissed tips.
    • Instances that are running are refused, because a running Claude would write its list back.
    • apply and sync warn when they add environments to an instance that needs this.

  • project remove keeps a folder trusted if another project or the instance's workdir still uses it.

Shared CLAUDE.md

Each instance has its own Claude Code config directory, so it doesn't read your ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. memory links that file into every instance, so your global instructions are the same everywhere and you edit them in one place:

claude-orchestrator memory status          # which instances are linked
claude-orchestrator memory link            # link every instance
claude-orchestrator memory link --force    # also replace an instance's own CLAUDE.md (kept as a backup)
claude-orchestrator memory unlink          # remove the links

New instances, and instances started without a CLAUDE.md, are linked automatically. An instance's own CLAUDE.md is never overwritten without --force.

Sessions

Each instance has its own Claude Code config directory, so its sessions stay with it. The session commands move them around:

claude-orchestrator session list                          # every instance, newest first
claude-orchestrator session list --instance work --project ~/workspace/api
claude-orchestrator session show 3f2a                     # an id prefix is enough
claude-orchestrator session copy 3f2a --to school         # the source keeps its copy
claude-orchestrator session move 3f2a --to school         # the source copy goes to a backup
claude-orchestrator session last --from work --to school  # move work's latest session
  • The name default means the Claude install outside claude-orchestrator (~/.claude), so session copy <id> --instance default --to work brings in an existing session.
  • The target must be stopped (or pass --force). move also needs the source to be stopped.
  • A session id that already exists in the target is refused unless you pass --force. So is a project folder that maps to the same directory name as a different path.
  • Files are copied to a temporary name and then renamed into place, so an interrupted transfer never leaves half a transcript. move doesn't delete anything. It moves the source files to ~/Library/Application Support/claude-ctl/backups/<time>-<id>/.
  • The transcript, sub-agent transcripts, TODO files and the project's sessions-index.json entry are all transferred. The session can be resumed with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<target>/claude-code claude --resume <id> (session show prints the exact command).
  • Claude Desktop's sidebar (experimental). If the source has a Desktop entry for the session and the target is signed in, a copy is written to the target's Code tab list. Account-specific fields are dropped. The entry appears after the target instance restarts. When the target's account is unknown, you get the --resume command instead.
  • Summaries are cached in ~/Library/Application Support/claude-ctl/cache/sessions.json, keyed by file size and modification time. The cache is safe to delete.

Chats in the Chat tab are not transferred. They are stored in your claude.ai account, not on disk, so an instance signed in to the same account already sees them and an instance signed in to a different account cannot open them.

Interactive move

Run session move with no arguments to pick everything on screen:

claude-orchestrator session move
  1. Pick the session. Type to fuzzy-filter by title, account or project folder (case and Turkish letters are ignored), move with ↑/↓ (or Ctrl-P/Ctrl-N), press Enter.
  2. Pick the target account. Every account except the session's owner is listed. This screen is skipped when there is only one other account.
  3. Confirm. The Claude instances of both accounts that are running are shut down one after the other, the session is moved, and they are reopened. Press y to go ahead; Esc goes back a screen.

session move <id> opens only the screens it still needs, and --to / --instance narrow the choice; --yes skips the confirmation. Passing both an id and --to keeps the old, non-interactive behaviour. Run it from a regular terminal: started from inside an instance it would have to shut down (a Code tab terminal), it refuses.

Menu bar agent

claude-orchestrator agent --install     # login item
claude-orchestrator agent               # run now

Each instance gets a menu bar icon (Claude's icon plus a badge). The menu can start a stopped instance, bring a running one to the front, stop it, open its workdir or profile folder, show its logs and display the sign-in guide. The agent is a single process; it refreshes every 5 seconds.

How it works

claude-orchestrator start runs exactly this:

open -n -a /Applications/Claude.app \
     --env  CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/Library/Application\ Support/claude-ctl/instances/<name>/claude-code \
     --args --user-data-dir=~/Library/Application\ Support/claude-ctl/instances/<name>/profile

-n asks macOS for a new application instance, so the second Claude does not join the first one. The per-instance data path comes from Claude's own Electron profile, and the Claude Code CLI is redirected with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

--env must come before --args: everything after --args is handed to the app as argv, so a misplaced --env would reach Claude as a stray argument instead of being consumed by open.

Before starting, the instance profile is seeded so the Code tab opens in the right project:

  • claude_desktop_config.json → preferences.localAgentModeTrustedFolders
  • ccd-session-presets.json → a session preset whose target.cwd is your workdir

Where things live

~/Library/Application Support/claude-ctl/
├── config.json                     # instance definitions
├── backups/                        # sources of `session move`
├── cache/sessions.json             # session summary cache
└── instances/<name>/
    ├── profile/                    # Electron profile
    ├── claude-code/                # CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
    └── state.json                  # pid, start time, Claude version

Known limitations

  • No separate Dock icon. Every instance shows Claude's icon; the menu bar agent's badges are what tell them apart. Giving an instance its own Dock icon requires changing the app's bundle identity, which breaks macOS/Electron security guarantees.
  • The application menu still says "Claude" (the name is compiled into the app).
  • Log files are shared. Claude writes to ~/Library/Logs/Claude/; claude-orchestrator logs filters by the instance's start time, so the separation is approximate.
  • The session preset needs an account. The workdir is seeded as a trusted folder immediately, but the "session preset" (the entry the Code tab opens with) is written only once the instance knows your Anthropic account — that is, after the first sign-in. Run claude-orchestrator signin <name> --restart (or restart the instance once) afterwards.
  • One claude:// handler. The OAuth deep link is delivered to a single instance; use claude-orchestrator signin <name> --exclusive. It also warns when the regular, non-instance Claude is open, since that one can catch the link too.
  • Disk usage. Each instance keeps its own Claude Code CLI download (~500 MB) plus its profile.
  • The Claude Code directory fills up after sign-in. The per-instance claude-code/ folder stays empty until the instance is signed in, because the CLI only starts once you use a Claude Code session in that instance.
  • Claude Desktop itself enforces some single-instance behaviour; if an instance refuses to start, claude-orchestrator doctor <name> explains why.

Development

swift build
swift test
./Scripts/smoke.sh     # live end-to-end check (starts real Claude instances)

To pick a version or a directory, set CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_VERSION=0.2.2 or CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_DIR=~/bin in front of sh. To uninstall, run curl -fsSL …/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall. Instance data is kept. Homebrew Recent Homebrew versions refuse to load formulae from a third-party tap until you trust it. Trust the tap before installing: brew tap yuix-networks/tap brew trust yuix-networks/tap brew install yuix-networks/tap/claude-orchestrator The formula lives in Yuix-Networks/homebrew-tap. Upgrade later with brew upgrade claude-orchestrator. From a release Download claude-orchestrator-<version>.tar.gz from Releases, extract it and put the binary on your PATH. From source swift build -c release cp .build/release/claude-orchestrator /usr/local/bin/ Requirements: macOS 13 (Ventura) or later — open --env is needed to pass the per-instance environment. Claude Desktop must be installed in /Applications. Commands Command What it does claude-orchestrator Interactive menu: profiles, sessions, projects (see Interactive mode) claude-orchestrator version Print the version claude-orchestrator new <name> [--workdir <path>] [--sessions-from <instance>] Create an instance; optionally seed a default project and copy another instance's sessions claude-orchestrator start <name> [--folder <path>] Start the instance (separate profile + config) claude-orchestrator stop <name> Stop the instance (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL if needed) claude-orchestrator list [--json] All instances with state, pid and workdir claude-orchestrator status <name> [--json] Details for one instance claude-orchestrator logs <name> [-n N] [-f] Instance log lines (-f follows, survives log rotation) claude-orchestrator open <name> [--target workdir|profile] Open a folder in Finder claude-orchestrator signin <name> [--restart] [--exclusive] Sign-in guide; --exclusive closes the other instances while you sign in claude-orchestrator doctor [<name>] [--json] Health checks: app version, profile, lock, disk, workdir, session claude-orchestrator clone <name> --as <new> [--workdir <path>] Copy an instance with its profile, config and sessions claude-orchestrator project apply [<file>] Apply a hand-edited projects.json to every instance claude-orchestrator memory link|unlink|status Share ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md with every instance claude-orchestrator project … (alias env) Projects shared by every instance — Claude Desktop calls them environments (see below) claude-orchestrator session … List, inspect, copy and move Claude Code sessions (see below) claude-orchestrator remove <name> [--purge [--permanent]] [--force] [--yes] Delete the instance (alias delete, rm). --purge moves its data to the Trash and --permanent deletes it for good. A running instance is stopped after you confirm, or right away with --force claude-orchestrator agent [--install|--uninstall] Menu bar icons (one per instance), installable as a login item Every --json output carries a schemaVersion field (currently 1). It is bumped only when a field is removed or renamed. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 runtime error, 2 usage error. Projects (environments) in every instance Claude Desktop keeps the Code tab's environments per profile and per account. Without help, you'd create every project again in each instance. project keeps one list and writes it into all of them: claude-orchestrator project add ~/workspace/api # name = folder name claude-orchestrator project add ~/workspace/site --name "Site" --folder ~/workspace/shared claude-orchestrator project import --from default # take over the regular Claude's environments claude-orchestrator project list # ✓ synced ✗ missing … waiting for sign-in claude-orchestrator project sync # re-apply to every instance claude-orchestrator project remove "Site" # also removes it from the instances (--keep: don't) The list lives in config.json. New instances get it automatically, and every start applies it again. Keeping the list in a file You can edit the list by hand in a JSON file and apply it, from the menu (Projects… → Apply a projects.json…, see Setting up projects from a JSON file) or with project apply. The default file is ~/.config/claude-orchestrator/projects.json. A fully commented example is in examples/projects.json. The smallest useful file: { "projects": [ { "name": "shop", "path": "~/workspace/shop/shop-backend", "folders": ["~/workspace/shop/shop-frontend"] }, { "path": "~/workspace/blog" } ] } claude-orchestrator project export ~/.config/claude-orchestrator/projects.json # start from what you have claude-orchestrator project apply --dry-run # show the plan, change nothing claude-orchestrator project apply # add, update and rename projects claude-orchestrator project apply --prune # also delete projects that are no longer in the file name and folders are optional. Paths may use ~ or be relative to the file. defaults applies to every project. defaults.folders is added to each project's extra folders (for example a knowledge-base repo every session should see), and defaults.permissionMode is used where a project doesn't set its own: { "defaults": { "folders": ["~/workspace/notes"], "permissionMode": "bypassPermissions" }, "projects": [ { "path": "~/workspace/blog", "permissionMode": "acceptEdits" } ] } permissionMode sets the default permission mode for sessions started in that project's folder. It can be default, acceptEdits, plan, auto or bypassPermissions. Claude Desktop stores this per account and per folder. For bypassPermissions, apply also turns on "allow bypass mode" and records the account's opt-in. An organization policy that disables bypass mode is left alone, and the output names the affected accounts. Removing permissionMode from the file clears it from Desktop. A change that only touches the mode keeps the environment's other settings. // comments and trailing commas are accepted. The whole file is checked first: every missing folder, duplicate name and misspelled key is reported together, and nothing changes until the file is clean. Without --prune, projects missing from the file stay registered. The plan lists them. A project whose folder, extra folders or name changed has its environment rewritten in every instance. That resets Desktop settings such as the model for that environment. An environment belongs to an account, so before the first sign-in only the folder is trusted. The environment itself is written on the first start after you sign in. In a profile that has seen several accounts, every account gets the project. An environment that already exists for the same folder is left alone, including its name, model and other settings. Claude reads the list file only once per account. Claude Desktop keeps environments in its own UI storage (the profile's Local Storage). It imports ccd-session-presets.json the first time the account opens in that profile, then overwrites the file with its own list. So: Projects written before the first sign-in show up on their own. In an instance that has already been opened, stop it and run claude-orchestrator project sync --reset-desktop (or project apply --reset-desktop). This moves the profile's Local Storage to Local Storage.bak-<time> and writes the full list, and Claude imports it on the next start. Sign-in is not affected, since cookies live elsewhere. The instance does lose its UI preferences, such as sidebar layout and dismissed tips. Instances that are running are refused, because a running Claude would write its list back. apply and sync warn when they add environments to an instance that needs this. project remove keeps a folder trusted if another project or the instance's workdir still uses it. Shared CLAUDE.md Each instance has its own Claude Code config directory, so it doesn't read your ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. memory links that file into every instance, so your global instructions are the same everywhere and you edit them in one place: claude-orchestrator memory status # which instances are linked claude-orchestrator memory link # link every instance claude-orchestrator memory link --force # also replace an instance's own CLAUDE.md (kept as a backup) claude-orchestrator memory unlink # remove the links New instances, and instances started without a CLAUDE.md, are linked automatically. An instance's own CLAUDE.md is never overwritten without --force. Sessions Each instance has its own Claude Code config directory, so its sessions stay with it. The session commands move them around: claude-orchestrator session list # every instance, newest first claude-orchestrator session list --instance work --project ~/workspace/api claude-orchestrator session show 3f2a # an id prefix is enough claude-orchestrator session copy 3f2a --to school # the source keeps its copy claude-orchestrator session move 3f2a --to school # the source copy goes to a backup claude-orchestrator session last --from work --to school # move work's latest session The name default means the Claude install outside claude-orchestrator (~/.claude), so session copy <id> --instance default --to work brings in an existing session. The target must be stopped (or pass --force). move also needs the source to be stopped. A session id that already exists in the target is refused unless you pass --force. So is a project folder that maps to the same directory name as a different path. Files are copied to a temporary name and then renamed into place, so an interrupted transfer never leaves half a transcript. move doesn't delete anything. It moves the source files to ~/Library/Application Support/claude-ctl/backups/<time>-<id>/. The transcript, sub-agent transcripts, TODO files and the project's sessions-index.json entry are all transferred. The session can be resumed with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<target>/claude-code claude --resume <id> (session show prints the exact command). Claude Desktop's sidebar (experimental). If the source has a Desktop entry for the session and the target is signed in, a copy is written to the target's Code tab list. Account-specific fields are dropped. The entry appears after the target instance restarts. When the target's account is unknown, you get the --resume command instead. Summaries are cached in ~/Library/Application Support/claude-ctl/cache/sessions.json, keyed by file size and modification time. The cache is safe to delete. Chats in the Chat tab are not transferred. They are stored in your claude.ai account, not on disk, so an instance signed in to the same account already sees them and an instance signed in to a different account cannot open them. Interactive move Run session move with no arguments to pick everything on screen: claude-orchestrator session move Pick the session. Type to fuzzy-filter by title, account or project folder (case and Turkish letters are ignored), move with ↑/↓ (or Ctrl-P/Ctrl-N), press Enter. Pick the target account. Every account except the session's owner is listed. This screen is skipped when there is only one other account. Confirm. The Claude instances of both accounts that are running are shut down one after the other, the session is moved, and they are reopened. Press y to go ahead; Esc goes back a screen. session move <id> opens only the screens it still needs, and --to / --instance narrow the choice; --yes skips the confirmation. Passing both an id and --to keeps the old, non-interactive behaviour. Run it from a regular terminal: started from inside an instance it would have to shut down (a Code tab terminal), it refuses. Menu bar agent claude-orchestrator agent --install # login item claude-orchestrator agent # run now Each instance gets a menu bar icon (Claude's icon plus a badge). The menu can start a stopped instance, bring a running one to the front, stop it, open its workdir or profile folder, show its logs and display the sign-in guide. The agent is a single process; it refreshes every 5 seconds. How it works claude-orchestrator start runs exactly this: open -n -a /Applications/Claude.app \ --env CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/Library/Application\ Support/claude-ctl/instances/<name>/claude-code \ --args --user-data-dir=~/Library/Application\ Support/claude-ctl/instances/<name>/profile -n asks macOS for a new application instance, so the second Claude does not join the first one. The per-instance data path comes from Claude's own Electron profile, and the Claude Code CLI is redirected with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. --env must come before --args: everything after --args is handed to the app as argv, so a misplaced --env would reach Claude as a stray argument instead of being consumed by open. Before starting, the instance profile is seeded so the Code tab opens in the right project: claude_desktop_config.json → preferences.localAgentModeTrustedFolders ccd-session-presets.json → a session preset whose target.cwd is your workdir Where things live ~/Library/Application Support/claude-ctl/ ├── config.json # instance definitions ├── backups/ # sources of `session move` ├── cache/sessions.json # session summary cache └── instances/<name>/ ├── profile/ # Electron profile ├── claude-code/ # CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR └── state.json # pid, start time, Claude version Known limitations No separate Dock icon. Every instance shows Claude's icon; the menu bar agent's badges are what tell them apart. Giving an instance its own Dock icon requires changing the app's bundle identity, which breaks macOS/Electron security guarantees. The application menu still says "Claude" (the name is compiled into the app). Log files are shared. Claude writes to ~/Library/Logs/Claude/; claude-orchestrator logs filters by the instance's start time, so the separation is approximate. The session preset needs an account. The workdir is seeded as a trusted folder immediately, but the "session preset" (the entry the Code tab opens with) is written only once the instance knows your Anthropic account — that is, after the first sign-in. Run claude-orchestrator signin <name> --restart (or restart the instance once) afterwards. One claude:// handler. The OAuth deep link is delivered to a single instance; use claude-orchestrator signin <name> --exclusive. It also warns when the regular, non-instance Claude is open, since that one can catch the link too. Disk usage. Each instance keeps its own Claude Code CLI download (~500 MB) plus its profile. The Claude Code directory fills up after sign-in. The per-instance claude-code/ folder stays empty until the instance is signed in, because the CLI only starts once you use a Claude Code session in that instance. Claude Desktop itself enforces some single-instance behaviour; if an instance refuses to start, claude-orchestrator doctor <name> explains why. content_html_zh:
Run Claude Desktop as many independent instances as you want on macOS — each with its own profile, account, sessions, Claude Code config and working directory.

claude-orchestrator never copies, patches or re-signs /Applications/Claude.app. It launches the original, signed app with a different data directory, so code signature, notarization, permissions and the built-in updater all keep working.

claude-orchestrator new work --workdir ~/workspace/my-project
claude-orchestrator start work
claude-orchestrator list

Or run claude-orchestrator with no arguments and do all of it from a menu (see Interactive mode).

Renamed in v0.2.0: claude-ctl is now claude-orchestrator, because the tool manages sessions as well as instances. The data directory stays at ~/Library/Application Support/claude-ctl/, so existing instances keep working.

Quick start: one instance per account

Keep work, school and a second work account signed in side by side:

claude-orchestrator new work
claude-orchestrator new school
claude-orchestrator new client --workdir ~/workspace/client   # optional default project

claude-orchestrator signin work --exclusive     # sign in, one instance at a time
claude-orchestrator signin school --exclusive
claude-orchestrator signin client --exclusive

claude-orchestrator project import --from default   # reuse the projects you already have
claude-orchestrator project add ~/workspace/api       # or add new ones: every instance gets them

claude-orchestrator start work && claude-orchestrator start school && claude-orchestrator start client
claude-orchestrator agent --install             # menu bar icons to start/stop/switch

signin --exclusive closes the other instances while you sign in, because the browser hands the login back through a single claude:// link that only one running Claude can receive. It reopens them when you press Enter.

Interactive mode

Run the command with no arguments in a terminal:

claude-orchestrator

Everything day-to-day can be done from the menu. You don't need to remember commands, session ids or file paths:

Claude Orchestrator
───────────────────────────────────────
❯ Work        ● running
  Personal    ● running
  School      ○ stopped   not logged in
───────────────────────────────────────
  + New profile
  Projects…

你能做什么

屏幕 选项
Home Every profile with running / stopped, and a warning when it is not logged in. Below them: + New profile and Projects…
Profile (logged in) Start, or Stop / Restart when it is running · Sessions… · Log in again…
Profile (not logged in) Log in only. The other options appear after you log in
Sessions… The profile's sessions, newest first. Type to fuzzy-filter by title, account or project folder
A session Its details (account, project, start, last activity, messages, size, id) · Copy to… · Move to…
+ New profile Asks for a name, creates the profile and opens its menu so you can log in right away
Projects… The registered projects and their state in each profile · + Add project · Apply a projects.json… · Export to a projects.json… · Sync all profiles · Import from a profile…
A project Its folders, permission mode and per-profile state · Remove…

Keys: ↑/↓ (or Ctrl-P / Ctrl-N) to move, Enter to choose, Esc to go back (in a search box, Esc clears the text first), q on the home screen to quit, Ctrl-U to clear a search or text field, Ctrl-C to cancel.

What happens behind the screens:

  • Log in / Log in again… run the signin --exclusive flow. After you confirm, the other running instances are closed while you log in, so the browser's claude:// link comes back to the right window. They are reopened when you press Enter. Use Log in again… when a login has expired or the profile should use a different account.
  • Copy to… / Move to… ask for the target account (skipped when there is only one other account), then show what will happen and wait for y. Instances that have to be closed are shut down one after the other, the session is transferred, and they are reopened even if the transfer fails. A copy closes only the target and the source keeps its session. A move closes both and keeps the original as a backup.
  • Anything that writes (logging in, transfers, project changes) asks for confirmation first, then prints the same report as the matching command and waits for Enter.
  • The menu refuses to close an instance it is running inside (for example a terminal in Claude's Code tab), because that would end the menu halfway through. Run it from a regular terminal such as Terminal or iTerm.

Setting up projects from a JSON file

A project is a folder that shows up as an environment in the Code tab of every profile. Instead of adding them one by one, describe them in a file and apply it:

  1. Copy the example file and edit the paths: mkdir -p ~/.config/claude-orchestrator cp examples/projects.json ~/.config/claude-orchestrator/projects.json examples/projects.json shows every option: a minimal entry, a custom name, extra folders, a per-project permission mode and shared defaults. If you already have projects, Projects… → Export to a projects.json… writes them to the file so you can start from there.
  2. Open Projects… → Apply a projects.json…. The default path is already filled in. Press Enter.
  3. Check the preview. The file is checked as a whole first, and every problem (a missing folder, a duplicate name, a misspelled key) is listed at once. Nothing changes until the file is clean. Apply ~/.config/claude-orchestrator/projects.json + website ~/workspace/website + Mobile app ~/workspace/mobile/app ~ api → API - old-project (not in the file) ❯ Apply changes Apply and remove the 1 not in the file Cancel + is added, ~ is changed or renamed, and - is registered but missing from the file. Apply changes keeps those. Apply and remove… deletes them, which makes the registry match the file exactly.
  4. The projects are written to every profile. A profile that has not logged in yet gets them on its first start after login. The Projects… list shows where each project stands: ✓ in sync, ✗ missing (fix it with Sync all profiles), … waiting for the first login.

The same file works without the menu (project apply --dry-run, project apply, project apply --prune). See Keeping the list in a file for the full format and the details of how Claude Desktop stores environments.

Trying it safely

Set CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_HOME to point any command, the menu included, at a separate data directory. You can then experiment without touching your real profiles:

CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_HOME=/tmp/co-test claude-orchestrator

Why

Claude Desktop stores everything in a single Electron profile, so a second launch either reuses the first one's session or refuses to start. Copying the app bundle works, but the copy falls behind on updates and has to be rebuilt every time.

claude-orchestrator uses the mechanism Claude already ships for this:

What How
Separate Electron profile (cookies, sessions, settings) --user-data-dir=<per-instance path>
Separate Claude Code config (~/.claude, sessions) CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<per-instance path>
Separate Dock tile open -n (new application instance)

The result: several Claude instances side by side, each working on a different project.

安装

Install script (recommended)

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Yuix-Networks/claude-orchestrator/main/install.sh | sh

The script downloads the latest release and checks its SHA-256 against the published value. It installs into /usr/local/bin when that is writable and into ~/.local/bin otherwise. It never uses sudo.

  • To pick a version or a directory, set CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_VERSION=0.2.2 or CLAUDE_ORCHESTRATOR_DIR=~/bin in front of sh.
  • To uninstall, run curl -fsSL …/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall. Instance data is kept.

自制

Recent Homebrew versions refuse to load formulae from a third-party tap until you trust it. Trust the tap before installing:

brew tap yuix-networks/tap
brew trust yuix-networks/tap
brew install yuix-networks/tap/claude-orchestrator

The formula lives in Yuix-Networks/homebrew-tap. Upgrade later with brew upgrade claude-orchestrator.

From a release

Download claude-orchestrator-<version>.tar.gz from Releases, extract it and put the binary on your PATH.

从源头

swift build -c release
cp .build/release/claude-orchestrator /usr/local/bin/

Requirements: macOS 13 (Ventura) or later — open --env is needed to pass the per-instance environment. Claude Desktop must be installed in /Applications.

命令

命令 它的作用
claude-orchestrator Interactive menu: profiles, sessions, projects (see Interactive mode)
claude-orchestrator version Print the version
claude-orchestrator new <name> [--workdir <path>] [--sessions-from <instance>] Create an instance; optionally seed a default project and copy another instance's sessions
claude-orchestrator start <name> [--folder <path>] Start the instance (separate profile + config)
claude-orchestrator stop <name> Stop the instance (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL if needed)
claude-orchestrator list [--json] All instances with state, pid and workdir
claude-orchestrator status <name> [--json] Details for one instance
claude-orchestrator logs <name> [-n N] [-f] Instance log lines (-f follows, survives log rotation)
claude-orchestrator open <name> [--target workdir|profile] Open a folder in Finder
claude-orchestrator signin <name> [--restart] [--exclusive] Sign-in guide; --exclusive closes the other instances while you sign in
claude-orchestrator doctor [<name>] [--json] Health checks: app version, profile, lock, disk, workdir, session
claude-orchestrator clone <name> --as <new> [--workdir <path>] Copy an instance with its profile, config and sessions
claude-orchestrator project apply [<file>] Apply a hand-edited projects.json to every instance
claude-orchestrator memory link|unlink|status Share ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md with every instance
claude-orchestrator project … (alias env) Projects shared by every instance — Claude Desktop calls them environments (see below)
claude-orchestrator session … List, inspect, copy and move Claude Code sessions (see below)
claude-orchestrator remove <name> [--purge [--permanent]] [--force] [--yes] Delete the instance (alias delete, rm). --purge moves its data to the Trash and --permanent deletes it for good. A running instance is stopped after you confirm, or right away with --force
claude-orchestrator agent [--install|--uninstall] Menu bar icons (one per instance), installable as a login item

Every --json output carries a schemaVersion field (currently 1). It is bumped only when a field is removed or renamed.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 runtime error, 2 usage error.

Projects (environments) in every instance

Claude Desktop keeps the Code tab's environments per profile and per account. Without help, you'd create every project again in each instance. project keeps one list and writes it into all of them:

claude-orchestrator project add ~/workspace/api                       # name = folder name
claude-orchestrator project add ~/workspace/site --name "Site" --folder ~/workspace/shared
claude-orchestrator project import --from default    # take over the regular Claude's environments
claude-orchestrator project list                     # ✓ synced  ✗ missing  … waiting for sign-in
claude-orchestrator project sync                     # re-apply to every instance
claude-orchestrator project remove "Site"            # also removes it from the instances (--keep: don't)
  • The list lives in config.json. New instances get it automatically, and every start applies it again.

Keeping the list in a file

You can edit the list by hand in a JSON file and apply it, from the menu (Projects… → Apply a projects.json…, see Setting up projects from a JSON file) or with project apply. The default file is ~/.config/claude-orchestrator/projects.json. A fully commented example is in examples/projects.json. The smallest useful file:

{
  "projects": [
    { "name": "shop", "path": "~/workspace/shop/shop-backend",
      "folders": ["~/workspace/shop/shop-frontend"] },
    { "path": "~/workspace/blog" }
  ]
}
claude-orchestrator project export ~/.config/claude-orchestrator/projects.json  # start from what you have
claude-orchestrator project apply --dry-run    # show the plan, change nothing
claude-orchestrator project apply              # add, update and rename projects
claude-orchestrator project apply --prune      # also delete projects that are no longer in the file
  • name and folders are optional. Paths may use ~ or be relative to the file.
  • defaults applies to every project. defaults.folders is added to each project's extra folders (for example a knowledge-base repo every session should see), and defaults.permissionMode is used where a project doesn't set its own: { "defaults": { "folders": ["~/workspace/notes"], "permissionMode": "bypassPermissions" }, "projects": [ { "path": "~/workspace/blog", "permissionMode": "acceptEdits" } ] }
  • permissionMode sets the default permission mode for sessions started in that project's folder. It can be default, acceptEdits, plan, auto or bypassPermissions. Claude Desktop stores this per account and per folder. For bypassPermissions, apply also turns on "allow bypass mode" and records the account's opt-in. An organization policy that disables bypass mode is left alone, and the output names the affected accounts. Removing permissionMode from the file clears it from Desktop. A change that only touches the mode keeps the environment's other settings.
  • // comments and trailing commas are accepted.
  • The whole file is checked first: every missing folder, duplicate name and misspelled key is reported together, and nothing changes until the file is clean.
  • Without --prune, projects missing from the file stay registered. The plan lists them.
  • A project whose folder, extra folders or name changed has its environment rewritten in every instance. That resets Desktop settings such as the model for that environment.
  • An environment belongs to an account, so before the first sign-in only the folder is trusted. The environment itself is written on the first start after you sign in. In a profile that has seen several accounts, every account gets the project.
  • An environment that already exists for the same folder is left alone, including its name, model and other settings.
  • Claude reads the list file only once per account. Claude Desktop keeps environments in its own UI storage (the profile's Local Storage). It imports ccd-session-presets.json the first time the account opens in that profile, then overwrites the file with its own list. So: Projects written before the first sign-in show up on their own. In an instance that has already been opened, stop it and run claude-orchestrator project sync --reset-desktop (or project apply --reset-desktop). This moves the profile's Local Storage to Local Storage.bak-<time> and writes the full list, and Claude imports it on the next start. Sign-in is not affected, since cookies live elsewhere. The instance does lose its UI preferences, such as sidebar layout and dismissed tips. Instances that are running are refused, because a running Claude would write its list back. apply and sync warn when they add environments to an instance that needs this.
  • project remove keeps a folder trusted if another project or the instance's workdir still uses it.

Shared CLAUDE.md

Each instance has its own Claude Code config directory, so it doesn't read your ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. memory links that file into every instance, so your global instructions are the same everywhere and you edit them in one place:

claude-orchestrator memory status          # which instances are linked
claude-orchestrator memory link            # link every instance
claude-orchestrator memory link --force    # also replace an instance's own CLAUDE.md (kept as a backup)
claude-orchestrator memory unlink          # remove the links

New instances, and instances started without a CLAUDE.md, are linked automatically. An instance's own CLAUDE.md is never overwritten without --force.

会议

Each instance has its own Claude Code config directory, so its sessions stay with it. The session commands move them around:

claude-orchestrator session list                          # every instance, newest first
claude-orchestrator session list --instance work --project ~/workspace/api
claude-orchestrator session show 3f2a                     # an id prefix is enough
claude-orchestrator session copy 3f2a --to school         # the source keeps its copy
claude-orchestrator session move 3f2a --to school         # the source copy goes to a backup
claude-orchestrator session last --from work --to school  # move work's latest session
  • The name default means the Claude install outside claude-orchestrator (~/.claude), so session copy <id> --instance default --to work brings in an existing session.
  • The target must be stopped (or pass --force). move also needs the source to be stopped.
  • A session id that already exists in the target is refused unless you pass --force. So is a project folder that maps to the same directory name as a different path.
  • Files are copied to a temporary name and then renamed into place, so an interrupted transfer never leaves half a transcript. move doesn't delete anything. It moves the source files to ~/Library/Application Support/claude-ctl/backups/<time>-<id>/.
  • The transcript, sub-agent transcripts, TODO files and the project's sessions-index.json entry are all transferred. The session can be resumed with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<target>/claude-code claude --resume <id> (session show prints the exact command).
  • Claude Desktop's sidebar (experimental). If the source has a Desktop entry for the session and the target is signed in, a copy is written to the target's Code tab list. Account-specific fields are dropped. The entry appears after the target instance restarts. When the target's account is unknown, you get the --resume command instead.
  • Summaries are cached in ~/Library/Application Support/claude-ctl/cache/sessions.json, keyed by file size and modification time. The cache is safe to delete.

Chats in the Chat tab are not transferred. They are stored in your claude.ai account, not on disk, so an instance signed in to the same account already sees them and an instance signed in to a different account cannot open them.

Interactive move

Run session move with no arguments to pick everything on screen:

claude-orchestrator session move
  1. Pick the session. Type to fuzzy-filter by title, account or project folder (case and Turkish letters are ignored), move with ↑/↓ (or Ctrl-P/Ctrl-N), press Enter.
  2. Pick the target account. Every account except the session's owner is listed. This screen is skipped when there is only one other account.
  3. Confirm. The Claude instances of both accounts that are running are shut down one after the other, the session is moved, and they are reopened. Press y to go ahead; Esc goes back a screen.

session move <id> opens only the screens it still needs, and --to / --instance narrow the choice; --yes skips the confirmation. Passing both an id and --to keeps the old, non-interactive behaviour. Run it from a regular terminal: started from inside an instance it would have to shut down (a Code tab terminal), it refuses.

Menu bar agent

claude-orchestrator agent --install     # login item
claude-orchestrator agent               # run now

Each instance gets a menu bar icon (Claude's icon plus a badge). The menu can start a stopped instance, bring a running one to the front, stop it, open its workdir or profile folder, show its logs and display the sign-in guide. The agent is a single process; it refreshes every 5 seconds.

它是如何运作的

claude-orchestrator start runs exactly this:

open -n -a /Applications/Claude.app \
     --env  CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/Library/Application\ Support/claude-ctl/instances/<name>/claude-code \
     --args --user-data-dir=~/Library/Application\ Support/claude-ctl/instances/<name>/profile

-n asks macOS for a new application instance, so the second Claude does not join the first one. The per-instance data path comes from Claude's own Electron profile, and the Claude Code CLI is redirected with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

--env must come before --args: everything after --args is handed to the app as argv, so a misplaced --env would reach Claude as a stray argument instead of being consumed by open.

Before starting, the instance profile is seeded so the Code tab opens in the right project:

  • claude_desktop_config.json → preferences.localAgentModeTrustedFolders
  • ccd-session-presets.json → a session preset whose target.cwd is your workdir

事物居住的地方

~/Library/Application Support/claude-ctl/
├── config.json                     # instance definitions
├── backups/                        # sources of `session move`
├── cache/sessions.json             # session summary cache
└── instances/<name>/
    ├── profile/                    # Electron profile
    ├── claude-code/                # CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
    └── state.json                  # pid, start time, Claude version

已知的限制

  • No separate Dock icon. Every instance shows Claude's icon; the menu bar agent's badges are what tell them apart. Giving an instance its own Dock icon requires changing the app's bundle identity, which breaks macOS/Electron security guarantees.
  • The application menu still says "Claude" (the name is compiled into the app).
  • Log files are shared. Claude writes to ~/Library/Logs/Claude/; claude-orchestrator logs filters by the instance's start time, so the separation is approximate.
  • The session preset needs an account. The workdir is seeded as a trusted folder immediately, but the "session preset" (the entry the Code tab opens with) is written only once the instance knows your Anthropic account — that is, after the first sign-in. Run claude-orchestrator signin <name> --restart (or restart the instance once) afterwards.
  • One claude:// handler. The OAuth deep link is delivered to a single instance; use claude-orchestrator signin <name> --exclusive. It also warns when the regular, non-instance Claude is open, since that one can catch the link too.
  • Disk usage. Each instance keeps its own Claude Code CLI download (~500 MB) plus its profile.
  • The Claude Code directory fills up after sign-in. The per-instance claude-code/ folder stays empty until the instance is signed in, because the CLI only starts once you use a Claude Code session in that instance.
  • Claude Desktop itself enforces some single-instance behaviour; if an instance refuses to start, claude-orchestrator doctor <name> explains why.
